Teach me CSS custom properties from beginner to advanced.

**CSS custom properties — Beginner to Expert**

[Beginner]
Define reusable values with `--name` and read them with `var(--name)`.
```css
:root { --brand: #2563eb; --radius: 8px; }
.button { background: var(--brand); border-radius: var(--radius); }
```
Why it works: variables cascade and inherit, so every `.button` reads the root values.

[Intermediate]
Override variables per scope and use fallbacks in `var()`.
```css
.card--dark { --bg: #1f2937; --text: #f9fafb; }
.card { background: var(--bg, #fff); color: var(--text, #111); }
```
Why it works: the more specific scope replaces the value for its subtree only; fallbacks guard against typos.

[Advanced]
Compute with `calc()`, switch themes with one attribute, and animate registered properties.
```css
[data-theme='dark'] { --bg: #0f172a; --text: #e2e8f0; }
.panel { padding: calc(var(--space, 1rem) * 2); background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); }
```
Why it works: a single attribute on `<html>` re-themes the entire tree with no JS repaint loops.

[Expert]
Pass values from JS to CSS and build fluid type with `clamp()`.
```js
document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--accent', '#22c55e');
```
```css
h1 { font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 1rem + 3vw, 3rem); }
```
Why it works: one source of truth feeds both languages, and `clamp()` keeps sizing fluid between bounds.

Add Open Graph and Twitter card tags so shared links preview nicely on social media.

```html
<head>
  <meta property="og:type" content="website">
  <meta property="og:site_name" content="Arion Hosting">
  <meta property="og:title" content="Managed WordPress Hosting That Just Works">
  <meta property="og:description"
        content="Automatic backups, global CDN, 24/7 human support.">
  <meta property="og:url" content="https://arionhost.example/plans">
  <meta property="og:image" content="https://arionhost.example/og-cover.png">
  <meta property="og:image:width" content="1200">
  <meta property="og:image:height" content="630">
  <meta property="og:image:alt" content="Arion Hosting dashboard on a laptop">

  <meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">
  <meta name="twitter:title" content="Managed WordPress Hosting That Just Works">
  <meta name="twitter:description" content="Backups, CDN, real support.">
  <meta name="twitter:image" content="https://arionhost.example/og-cover.png">
</head>
```

**Why this works:** Social platforms do not execute your JavaScript or read `<title>` for previews — their crawlers parse Open Graph (`og:`) meta tags server-side. `og:image` must be an absolute URL, and declaring `width`/`height` (1200×630 is the sweet spot) prevents cropped or rejected previews. `twitter:card="summary_large_image"` opts into the big-image layout on X/Twitter; Twitter falls back to the `og:` values when its own tags are missing, but explicit tags give you per-platform control of the copy. Because these crawlers rarely run JS, tags like these must be in the raw server-rendered HTML, not injected client-side.

Debug this: the google font never applies.

**Symptom:** The Google Font never applies.

**Root cause:** The stylesheet URL is malformed, preconnect is missing crossorigin, or the family name/weights are wrong; also check the CSS cascade overrides it later.

**Fix:**
```css
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<style>body { font-family: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif; }</style>
```

**Broken version:**
```css
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Inter" rel="stylesheet"> /* old API + no display */
```

**Prevention:** Open DevTools → Network → filter 'font' to confirm the woff2 files download, and verify the exact family name.

localStorage چیه و چه فرقی با sessionStorage داره؟ لطفاً به انگلیسی جواب بده.

Both are browser storage APIs that persist key/value strings client-side.

- **localStorage** — survives page reloads and browser restarts, never expires, and is shared across all tabs of the same origin.
- **sessionStorage** — scoped to a single tab and cleared automatically when that tab closes.

```js
localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark');
localStorage.getItem('theme');   // 'dark'
localStorage.removeItem('theme');
localStorage.clear();
```

Common uses: localStorage for themes, language preference and drafts; sessionStorage for one-time tokens or multi-step form state.

Limits to keep in mind: about 5 MB per origin, strings only (use `JSON.stringify` / `JSON.parse`), synchronous API (huge writes can block the main thread), and never store secrets there — any script running on the page can read it.
